newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, December 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, December 3.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said he believed the government would fall next spring when it became clear the 1997 budget would not allow Italy to meet the criteria for EMU. If this happened, Berlusconi said he would offer to lead a broad coalition government to oversee constitutional and institutional reforms for a set period of time (all).
* Prime Minister Romano Prodi says: "The government is in good shape and is going ahead." Leftist party PDS rejects Berlusconi's proposal of a new broad coalition government (all).
* Ministers are due to meet today to discuss the parliamentary passage of the 1997 budget (all).

* Italy's cumulative public sector borrowing requirement was 135.3 trillion lire at end November 1996, about one trillion lire less than during the same period last year, but largely overshooting the government forecasts of a 123 trillion lire deficit for 1996. An additional budget in 1997 spring looks likely (all).

* State-owned credit institute Mediocredito Centrale engaged itself to submit a formal offer for loss-making Banco di Napoli. Insurance group INA and Treasury-controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, who have expressed joint interest in making a bid, preferred to delay the decision. The European Commission reportedly would not oppose a bid from a state-controlled institute (Sole 24 Ore).

* Monaco-based businessman Luigi Giribaldi has raised his stake in Carlo De Benedetti's financial holding group Cofide to 20.05 percent. Giribaldi's stake is held through the Monaco-based Banque du Gothard (all).

* Media group Cecchi Gori, which owns two television channels, is looking for new partners to strengthen the third television force in Italy. But the group is waiting for new controversial telecom regulations, which are under discussion in parliament (Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
